summary:
[  edit  ]
The Copy  SOP  lets you make copies of the geometry of other SOPs and apply a transformation to each copy.
It also allows you to copy geometry to points on an input template.

parameters.label: Source  Group
parameters.name: sourcegrp
parameters.description: Specifies a subset of input primitives to copy from. Accepts patterns, as described in  Pattern Matching .

parameters.label: Template  Group
parameters.name: templategrp
parameters.description: Specifies a subset of template primitives from which to copy onto. Accepts patterns, as described in  Pattern Matching .

parameters.label: Number of Copies
parameters.name: ncy
parameters.description: Sets number of Copies to be made of the source. For a template input, it specifies the number of copies to be placed at each point of the template.

parameters.label: Primitives per  Point
parameters.name: nprims
parameters.description: Defines how many primitives to copy from each point.

parameters.label: Rotate to Normal
parameters.name: nml
parameters.description: Only used when a template input is specified. If the template is a sphere, and the first input is a circle, a circle is placed at each point of the sphere. With this option on, all the circles will re-orient to face the surface of the sphere (a default sphere has normals radiating outwards from the center).

parameters.label: Transform Cumulative
parameters.name: cum
parameters.description: Each transformation "builds" on the location left by the one before it. Transformations are cumulative as the Copy  SOP  produces new copies.

parameters.label: Transform Order
parameters.name: xord
parameters.description: ⊞  - Sets the overall transform order for the transformations. The  Transform Order  determines the order in which transformations take place. Depending on the order, you can achieve different results using the exact same values. Choose the appropriate order from the menu.

parameters.label: Rotate Order
parameters.name: rord
parameters.description: ⊞  - Sets the order of the rotations within the overall transform order.

parameters.label: Translate
parameters.name: t
parameters.description: ⊞  - These allow you to specify the Translation (how much it moves over in a given direction), Rotation, and the Scale between each copy. Three columns are given for X, Y, and Z coordinates. Guide geometry is provided for the Pivot's translations. The Pivot is represented by a single red dot in the Viewport. Changing the Pivot parameters moves this point of reference.

parameters.label: Rotate
parameters.name: r
parameters.description: ⊞  - These allow you to specify the Translation (how much it moves over in a given direction), Rotation, and the Scale between each copy. Three columns are given for X, Y, and Z coordinates. Guide geometry is provided for the Pivot's translations. The Pivot is represented by a single red dot in the Viewport. Changing the Pivot parameters moves this point of reference.

parameters.label: Scale
parameters.name: s
parameters.description: ⊞  - These allow you to specify the Translation (how much it moves over in a given direction), Rotation, and the Scale between each copy. Three columns are given for X, Y, and Z coordinates. Guide geometry is provided for the Pivot's translations. The Pivot is represented by a single red dot in the Viewport. Changing the Pivot parameters moves this point of reference.

parameters.label: Pivot
parameters.name: p
parameters.description: ⊞  - These allow you to specify the Translation (how much it moves over in a given direction), Rotation, and the Scale between each copy. Three columns are given for X, Y, and Z coordinates. Guide geometry is provided for the Pivot's translations. The Pivot is represented by a single red dot in the Viewport. Changing the Pivot parameters moves this point of reference.

parameters.label: Uniform Scale
parameters.name: scale
parameters.description: Uniform Scale allows you to shrink or enlarge geometry along all three axes simultaneously.

parameters.label: Normals Maintain Length
parameters.name: vlength
parameters.description: Vector type attributes (i.e. normals, velocity) maintain the same length under transforms. i.e. When geometry is scaled, the normals remain constant in length.

parameters.label: Create Output Groups
parameters.name: newg
parameters.description: If selected, this creates a group for each copy number, and places each primitive created at that stage into it.

parameters.label: Copy Groups
parameters.name: copyg
parameters.description: Defines the base name of the groups created.

parameters.label: Look At
parameters.name: lookat
parameters.description: Orients the copied geometry to lookat, or point to, the  object  component specified in the parameter.

parameters.label: Up Vector
parameters.name: upvector
parameters.description: ⊞  - When specifying a Look At, it is possible to specify an up vector for the lookat. Without using an up vector, it is possible to get poor animation when the lookat object passes through the Y axis of the target object.

parameters.label: Stamp Inputs
parameters.name: stamp
parameters.description: When enabled, it will Stamp proceeding variables for each input copied.

parameters.label: Copy
parameters.name: copy
parameters.description: Sequence of stamp variables

parameters.description: Token of each stamp variable. Stamped parameters are accessible via the global   fetchStamp  ()   method in the  td Module  in python, or  param()  in tscript. See the example, below.

parameters.label: Value
parameters.name: copy0value
parameters.description: Value of each stamp variable. Stamped parameters are accessible via the global   fetchStamp  ()   method in the  td Module  in python, or  param()  in tscript. See the example, below.

parameters.name: subpt
parameters.description: ⊞  - Subtract the attributes from the source geometry's point attributes.

parameters.name: subprim
parameters.description: ⊞  - Subtract the attributes from the source geometry's primitive attributes.

parameters.label: You can use the  me.copyTotal  python member to calculate the degrees of rotation for a given number of copies. For example, if you have 28 copies, you can set the rotation to be:  360/me.copyTotal
parameters.description: this would automatically give you 12.8571 degrees, evenly spacing your 28 copies around the full circumference of the circle.

parameters.description: Number of points in this  SOP .

parameters.label: last_vbo_update_time
parameters.description: Time spent in another thread updating geometry data on the  GPU  from the  SOP 's CPU data. As it is part of another thread, this time is not part of the usual frame time.

parameters.label: last_meta_vbo_update_time
parameters.description: Time spent in another thread updating meta surface geometry data (such as metaballs or nurbs) on the  GPU  from the  SOP 's CPU data. As it is part of another thread, this time is not part of the usual frame time.

parameters.label: total_cooks
parameters.description: Number of times the operator has cooked since the process started.

parameters.label: cook_time
parameters.description: Duration of the last cook in milliseconds.

parameters.label: cook_frame
parameters.description: Frame number when this operator was last cooked relative to the component timeline.

parameters.label: cook_abs_frame
parameters.description: Frame number when this operator was last cooked relative to the absolute time.

parameters.label: cook_start_time
parameters.description: Time in milliseconds at which the operator started cooking in the frame it was cooked.

parameters.label: cook_end_time
parameters.description: Time in milliseconds at which the operator finished cooking in the frame it was cooked.

parameters.label: cooked_this_frame
parameters.description: 1 if operator was cooked this frame.

parameters.label: warnings
parameters.description: Number of warnings in this operator if any.

parameters.label: errors
parameters.description: Number of errors in this operator if any.

Esto es eficiente porque los POPs ya implementan muchas funciones de CHOPs directamente en la GPU, evitando conversiones de GPU a CPU y viceversa. • Experimental:Circle POP: Un operador generador que crea formas circulares. Puede generar puntos con sus primitivas correspondientes. • Experimental:Convert POP: Se usa para cambiar entre diferentes tipos de primitivas. • Experimental:Copy POP: Permite crear copias de geometría dentro de un POP, las cuales pueden ser manipuladas o animadas antes de la renderización. triángulos** (`Quads to Triangles`). * Puede **abrir o cerrar** line strips. * Puede "aplanar" una geometría haciendo que los puntos de todas las primitivas sean **únicos** (no compartidos) y luego reordenando todos los puntos según el orden de los vértices de cada primitiva. Esto es útil para ciertos flujos de trabajo. * Importante: **No cambia los datos de los puntos** ni su orden, ni los vértices ni las primitivas en sí, solo cómo se "ven" organizados. --- #### 14. Copy POP * **¿Qué hace?** Este operador te permite **hacer copias de tu geometría de entrada**.
